data.title: Statistic
data.tagline: Highlight a small number of important values
data.description: A statistic combines a label, value, unit, and sometimes a trend. If a number went up or down, say what time period or baseline it is compared with. Keep formats and definitions consistent for money, percentages, counts, and other units.

avoid: Show a number without its label or unit
Use color alone to explain whether a change is good
Compare different time periods without saying so
Place so many statistics together that none stands out

lessonPractice.title: An operations dashboard reports 486 orders this week, up 12% from last week. How should it show the number and comparison clearly?

options.label: Emphasize 486 orders this week and add Up 12% from last week
options.feedback: Metric name, current value, unit, and benchmark are all explicit, so the change can be understood.

options.label: Show only a large ↑12% and omit the order count and comparison period
options.feedback: A percentage without the metric or comparison period cannot support a business judgment.

options.label: Use a 12% progress bar for weekly orders and let its length communicate performance
options.feedback: Progress needs a defined target. This data describes a count and period-over-period change, not completion.

data.agentPrompt: Present weekly orders as a statistic: show 486 orders as the main value and Up 12% from last week as context. Do not show an arrow or percentage alone. Handle no prior data, decline, and last-updated time.
